Chalet Hotels Limited July 30, 2026 Looking ahead, we have outlined a planned capex of approximately INR30 billion over FY27 to FY29 across our hospitality and commercial real estate portfolio.
Growth & demand: Leisure portfolio delivered a strong 19% RevPAR growth with a healthy mix of occupancy and ADR increase.

There have been also upgrades that have aided us in the revenue growth, like addition of Nox, a sky lounge that used to be a dead space and now clocks ~INR10 million a month in revenue within the first year of opening, addition of gaming and sports facilities, and more.
We delivered 9% growth in revenue year-on-year to INR4,185 million and 11% growth in EBITDA of INR1,784 million, a strong performance by any measure.
Margins & costs: Importantly, EBITDA margin improved by 231 bps to 46.7%.

Hospitality revenue grew by 9%, while EBITDA stood at INR1,784 million, up 11% year -on- year, reflecting 92 bps improvement in EBITDA margin on the back of resilient pricing dynamics and efficiency measures.
EBITDA margins expanded by 231 basis points to 46.7%, driven by strong performance across asset s and efficiency measures which we have implemented.
Capex & expansion: Several more changes are work in progress, including the widening of the approach road and the expansion of the banquet facility, which alone will 3x our facilities and become one of the largest in the MMR.
As I have mentioned, commissioning of CIGNUS II at our Powai complex in FY2027-28 will bring a major impetus to this business.
Net debt as o f June '26 stood at INR2 0,405 million, slightly higher versus March '26 as we completed few acquisitions.
Balance sheet & cash: The current yearly rentals potentially give us a leverage advantage of INR2,000 crores eligibility for LRD.
INR10,914 million of the net debt is actually allocable to assets under construction or which are yet to be operationalized.

The average cost of finance declined marginally to 7.4% as of June '26 versus 7.5% as of March '26, indicating strength of our treasury practices, leverage mix, ca sh flows, and overall balance sheet strength.
